questions.text: Under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, Scheduled Commercial Banks must maintain the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) on a fortnightly average basis. What is the minimum percentage of the total CRR requirement that a bank must maintain on a daily basis during the reporting fortnight?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate 50% and 60% (too low for daily floor). Eliminate 80% (was the requirement briefly in 2014 before reduction). The specific daily maintenance floor is 70%. Full Solution: As per RBI circular DBR.No.Ret.BC.71/12.01.001/2014-15 dated Feb 9, 2015, banks are required to maintain a minimum of 70% of their CRR requirement on all days of the fortnight, effective from the fortnight beginning Feb 14, 2015. The fortnightly average must be 100%.

questions.text: A grocer wants to mix two varieties of tea costing ₹ 60 per kg and ₹ 80 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹ 70 per kg. In what ratio must he mix them?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Alligation rule – Ratio = (Dearer − Mean) : (Mean − Cheaper) = (80 − 70) : (70 − 60) = 10 : 10 = 1 : 1. Full: Let x kg at ₹60 and y kg at ₹80. Then 60x + 80y = 70(x + y) ⇒ 10y = 10x ⇒ x : y = 1 : 1.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BANK' is written as 'CZOL'. If the same coding rule is applied, how will 'RBI' be written?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Observe that consonants are replaced by the next letter (B→C, N→O, K→L) while vowels are replaced by the previous letter (A→Z). Apply to RBI: R (consonant)→S, B (consonant)→C, I (vowel)→H, giving SCH. Step-by-step: Identify the pattern from BANK→CZOL: B+1=C, A-1=Z, N+1=O, K+1=L. Thus consonants shift forward, vowels shift backward. Using this, R→S, B→C, I→H, so RBI becomes SCH.

questions.text: In a certain coded language: 'P + Q' means 'P is the father of Q'; 'P - Q' means 'P is the mother of Q'; 'P * Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'; 'P / Q' means 'P is the sister of Q'; 'P % Q' means 'P is the husband of Q'; 'P $ Q' means 'P is the wife of Q'. Based on the above codes, in the expression **'P + Q - R * S % T'**, how is **P** related to **T**?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Generation Gap method. Trace generations: P(+1)→Q(+1)→R(0)→S(0)→T. Total gap = +2 (Grandparent level). Since the link to T is through marriage (S % T), add 'in-law'. P is male (+), so Grandfather-in-law. Full: P+Q (Father), Q-R (Mother) → P Grandfather of R. R*S (Brother) → P Grandfather of S. S%T (Husband) → T Wife of S. Thus P is Grandfather-in-law of T.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the expression \((347)^{89} \times (562)^{103} \times (789)^{56}\)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. Unit digit of 7^89: cycle 7,9,3,1 (length 4), 89%4=1 → 7. Unit digit of 2^103: cycle 2,4,8,6 (length 4), 103%4=3 → 8. Unit digit of 9^56: cycle 9,1 (length 2), 56%2=0 → 1. Multiply unit digits: 7×8×1 = 56 → unit digit 6. Step-by-step: 347^89 ends in 7^89. 7^4=2401 (ends in 1), so 7^88 ends in 1, 7^89 ends in 7. 562^103 ends in 2^103. 2^4=16 (ends in 6), 2^100 ends in 6, 2^103=2^100×8 ends in 8. 789^56 ends in 9^56. 9^2=81 (ends in 1), so 9^56 ends in 1. Final product unit digit = 7×8×1 = 56 → 6.

questions.text: Rahul starts from point A, walks 5 m north, then turns right and walks 12 m, then turns left and walks 5 m, and finally turns right and walks 12 m. What is the straight-line distance between his final position and point A?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The movements form a rectangle; total eastward displacement = 12+12 = 24 m, total northward displacement = 5+5 = 10 m. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse: √(24²+10²) = √676 = 26 m. Step-by-step: Starting at origin (0,0). North 5 → (0,5). Right (east) 12 → (12,5). Left (north) 5 → (12,10). Right (east) 12 → (24,10). Distance = √(24²+10²) = 26 m.

questions.text: The Government of India issues Treasury Bills (T-Bills) via the Reserve Bank of India to meet short-term borrowing requirements. Which of the following sets correctly identifies the three standard tenors of T-Bills currently auctioned in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options containing '14-day' (Cash Management Bills / WMA instruments, not regular T-Bills). Eliminate '273-day' (non-standard tenor). The only set with the three standard tenors (91, 182, 364 days) is Option B. Full Solution: The RBI, on behalf of GoI, currently issues T-Bills in three tenors: 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day. 14-day Intermediate T-Bills were discontinued in 2001. Cash Management Bills (CMBs) are issued for periods less than 91 days as needed.

questions.text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), an overdraft facility is available to eligible account holders after satisfactory operation of the account for six months. What is the current maximum permissible overdraft limit per household (typically the lady of the house) under this scheme?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate ₹5,000 (original limit at launch in 2014). Eliminate ₹15,000/₹20,000 (MUDRA Shishu/Kishor loan limits, commonly confused). The limit was doubled to ₹10,000 in 2018. Full Solution: The PMJDY scheme initially offered an OD limit of ₹5,000. In 2018, the Government enhanced the overdraft limit to ₹10,000 per household. There is no interest charged on OD up to ₹2,000; standard rates apply beyond that.

questions.text: As per the Reserve Bank of India's guidelines for Payments Banks (updated as of April 2021), what is the maximum end-of-day deposit balance permitted per individual customer?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options by magnitude. Payments Banks hold a restricted licence (no lending), so per-customer deposit caps are far below universal banks. ₹10L (D) and ₹5L (C) are implausibly high. ₹1L (A) was the original 2017 limit. The RBI raised this to ₹2L in April 2021 to enhance usability. Full Solution: Payments Banks were initially permitted a maximum end-of-day deposit balance of ₹1 lakh per customer (2017 Guidelines). To provide greater flexibility and encourage digital payments, the RBI, vide circular DBR.NBD.No.4502/16.13.218/2020-21 dated April 7, 2021, enhanced this limit to ₹2 lakh per customer with immediate effect. This limit applies to the aggregate balance across all accounts (savings/current) held by a customer in that Payments Bank.

questions.text: With effect from February 4, 2020, the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) revised the maximum insurance cover for depositors in insured banks. What is the current maximum deposit insurance cover payable per depositor per bank?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate ₹1 Lakh (pre-2020 limit). Eliminate ₹10 Lakh (often confused with EPFO EDLI limit). Eliminate ₹2 Lakh (intermittent proposal figure). The notified revision in 2020 fixed the cover at ₹5 Lakh. Full Solution: The DICGC (Amendment) Act, 2021, effective retrospectively from Feb 4, 2020, raised the deposit insurance cover from ₹1 Lakh to ₹5 Lakh per depositor per bank. This covers all commercial banks, SFBs, PBs, and eligible cooperative banks.

questions.text: The following sentence is divided into four parts labelled (A), (B), (C), and (D). One of these parts contains a grammatical error. Identify the erroneous part. "The number of loan applications received by the bank (A) / have increased significantly (B) / since the announcement of the new interest subvention scheme (C) / for the MSME sector. (D)"

options.label: A
options.text: The number of loan applications received by the bank

options.label: C
options.text: since the announcement of the new interest subvention scheme

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the 'The number of vs A number of' rule. 'The number of' takes a singular verb (has); 'A number of' takes a plural verb (have). Here, the subject is 'The number' (singular), so the verb must be 'has increased'. Full Solution: The subject of the verb is the singular noun phrase 'The number'. The prepositional phrase 'of loan applications...' modifies the subject but does not change its number. Therefore, the plural verb 'have increased' in part (B) is incorrect; it should be the singular 'has increased'. Parts (A), (C), and (D) are grammatically correct.

questions.text: Find the next term in the series: A2, C5, E9, G14, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Letters increase by 2 each step (A→C→E→G→I). Numbers increase by successive increments (+3,+4,+5→+6). Full solution: The letter sequence follows alternate alphabets: A(1), C(3), E(5), G(7) so next is I(9). The numeric sequence: 2, 5 (+3), 9 (+4), 14 (+5) so next increment is +6 giving 20. Thus the term is I20.

questions.text: In the following questions, two sentences (I) and (II) are given. Each sentence has a blank. Choose the pair of words that fits both blanks in the correct order (first word for I, second for II). I. The regulatory framework is designed to prevent ______ market conditions that could destabilize the banking sector. II. As a ______ observer, the ombudsman must remain impartial and base the verdict solely on documentary evidence.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Effect vs. Feeling' and 'Judge vs. Bored' rules. **Adverse** pairs with 'Effect/Condition' (external harm); **Averse** pairs with 'To' (internal feeling). **Disinterested** means impartial (like a Judge); **Uninterested** means bored. Step-by-step: Sentence I describes 'market conditions'. The standard collocation is 'adverse conditions' (harmful/unfavourable). 'Averse conditions' is incorrect usage (people are averse *to* things). Eliminate Options C and D. Sentence II describes an 'observer' who must be 'impartial'. 'Disinterested' means unbiased/impartial. 'Uninterested' means lacking interest. 'Disinterested observer' is the correct legal/formal term. Option B fits both blanks perfectly.

questions.text: As per the extant RBI Master Direction on Priority Sector Lending (PSL), which category of Scheduled Commercial Banks is mandated to allocate 75% of its Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE), whichever is higher, towards Priority Sector?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate PSBs and PVBs (uniform 40% target). Eliminate RRBs (75% target applies but on outstanding advances, not ANBC/CEOBE framework identically). SFBs have a distinct, higher 75% ANBC/CEOBE mandate. Full Solution: As per the RBI Master Direction on PSL (updated 2023), Small Finance Banks (SFBs) are required to maintain a PSL target of 75% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher. Domestic SCBs (PSBs/PVBs) have a 40% target. RRBs have a 75% target on total outstanding advances.

questions.text: Rohan walks 6 m towards North, then turns right and walks 8 m. He then turns left and walks 6 m, and finally turns right and walks 8 m. What is the straight-line distance between his final position and the starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The movements form a rectangle; net east displacement = 8+8=16 m, net north displacement = 6+6=12 m. Distance = √(16²+12²)=20 m (3-4-5 triple scaled by 4). Full solution: Starting at origin, after north 6 and right 8, position (8,6). Left turn (north) 6 → (8,12). Right turn (east) 8 → (16,12). Straight-line distance = √(16²+12²)=√400=20 m.
